title: Google Dots in Motion
slide_intent: Give system states distinguishable movements so people can tell whether a service is listening, processing or responding.
strategic_value: Four recurring colored dots can turn Google’s identity into useful feedback during an interaction.
demonstration: The animation labels listening, user speech, thinking and replying while dots shift into bars, clusters and a row; a later construction view reveals arc paths.
practical_value: Compare the movements assigned to different states and preserve the relationship between a state and its motion.

content_islands.name: State examples
content_islands.spec: Center the four colored shapes above a small state caption on a pale field.

content_islands.name: Path demonstration
content_islands.spec: Replace the examples with a guided arc construction showing coordinated dot movement.

reference_purposes.Intent: The article explicitly describes the dots as Google’s intelligence at work and feedback that Google is working for the user.
reference_purposes.Expression: Colored dots vary height, grouping and position across the labeled states.
reference_purposes.Application: The sequence maps the visual behaviors to listening, user speech, thinking and replying.

ingredient.name: Animated dots
ingredient.role: Communicate the current interaction state while retaining Google’s color identity.
ingredient.application: Assign distinct behavior to each state and coordinate the dots along consistent paths and easing, as described by the article.
ingredient.scope: The 2015 assistive identity demonstration. The clip is illustrative and does not provide production timing or easing values.
